Add dark mode toggle to the settings page

Objective

Add a toggle button to the user settings page (SettingsPage.tsx) that switches between light and dark mode. The preference is persisted in localStorage and applied via a data-theme attribute on document.documentElement. Toggling respects prefers-color-scheme as the initial default.

Context

Users have requested dark mode support. The design system already has dark-mode CSS variables under [data-theme="dark"] in src/styles/tokens.css, but there is no UI to toggle the theme. The settings page is the right home since it already has user-preference controls (language, timezone).

Steps

  1. Create src/hooks/useTheme.ts — a React hook that reads the initial theme from localStorage (fallback: prefers-color-scheme), writes changes back, and applies the data-theme attribute to document.documentElement.
    Why: Isolates theme persistence logic so the toggle component stays presentational.
    Verify
    Hook returns [theme, setTheme]; switching theme updates document.documentElement.dataset.theme and persists to localStorage.
  2. Create src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx — a <button> that calls useTheme, renders a sun/moon SVG icon, and has an accessible aria-label ("Switch to dark mode" / "Switch to light mode").
    Why: Accessible toggle button with semantic HTML — not a div with onClick.
    Verify
    Renders a <button> (not <div>); aria-label reflects current theme state; keyboard-activatable (Enter/Space).
  3. Add ThemeToggle to src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx in the Appearance section, alongside the existing language and timezone pickers.
    Why: Co-locates the toggle with other user preferences. The Appearance section already exists; no new section needed.
    Verify
    SettingsPage.tsx imports and renders ThemeToggle inside the .appearance-section div.
  4. Add unit tests in src/hooks/__tests__/useTheme.test.ts and src/components/__tests__/ThemeToggle.test.tsx.
    Why: Covers the toggle interaction, localStorage persistence, and initial prefers-color-scheme fallback.
    Verify
    npm test -- useTheme ThemeToggle passes; toggle renders with correct aria-label for each theme state.

Tests

Objective-verification test

File: src/components/__tests__/ThemeToggle.test.tsx

Asserts: Clicking the toggle switches document.documentElement.dataset.theme between light and dark; aria-label updates to match.

Run: npm test -- ThemeToggle

Unit test — useTheme hook

File: src/hooks/__tests__/useTheme.test.ts

Covers: initial value from localStorage, fallback to prefers-color-scheme, persistence on change.

Run: npm test -- useTheme

Acceptance Criteria

Verification

Load the settings page in Chrome with DevTools open. Click the toggle and confirm (1) document.documentElement.dataset.theme switches in the Elements panel, (2) the page styling changes visibly, (3) reloading the page preserves the selected theme. Tab to the toggle and confirm activation with Enter. Open the page with OS set to dark mode and confirm the default theme is dark.
